### a. Definitions {.unnumbered}

#### Classic causal inference








::: {#def-statistical-model .theorem}
## Statistical model

A *[statistical model](#def-statistical-model)* is a collection of probability distributions on a set of random variables.

$$
\mathcal{M}=\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\quad\text{on set of random variables }\mathbf V.
$$
:::

::: {#def-observational-unit .theorem}
## Observational unit

An *[observational unit](#def-observational-unit)* is a subset of the random variables in a [statistical model](#def-statistical-model) that originate from the same data source. The collection of observational units forms a partition of the full set of random variables. Define $n$ as the number of observational units then observations are sets $(V_i)$ such that: 

$$
\mathbf V=\bigcup_{i=1}^n \mathbf V_i,\qquad \mathbf V_i\cap \mathbf V_j=\varnothing\ (i\ne j).
$$
:::

::: {#def-equivalence .theorem}
## Equivalence

Two random variables are *equivalent* if they belong to different [observational units](#def-observational-unit) but represent the same construct. Two sets of random variables are equivalent if each element in one set has an equivalent in the other set.

$$
X_i\sim X_j\iff i\ne j;\ X_i\in \mathbf V_i;\ X_j\in \mathbf V_j,\ X_i, X_j \text{ represent same construct}.
$$
:::

::: {#def-npsem-ie .theorem}
## NPSEM-IE

A *nonparametric structural equation model with independent errors (NPSEM-IE)* specifies each random variable in a model as a deterministic function of other variables along with an error term. Error terms are mutually independent and the system of functions does not admit self-dependence cycles. They can be ordered to each be a function of earlier variables in the ordering. In a model of $p$ random variables. 

$$
V_{j} \;=\; f_{j}\!\big( V_{1},\dots,V_{j-1},\, U_{j} \big),
$$

$$
\{U_i\}_{j=1}^p \ \text{ mutually independent.}
$$
:::

::: {#def-parent-child .theorem}
## Parent/child/ancestor/descendant

In an [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie), if variable $X$ appears in the structural equation for $Y$, then $X$ is a *parent* of $Y$ and $Y$ is a *child* of $X$. The parent of a parent is an ancestor and the parent of an ancestor is an ancestor. If $X$ is an ancestor of $Y$, then $Y$ is a descendent of $X$. For a given variable $X$, the set of parents, children, ancestors, and descendants are denoted $\mathbf{Pa}(X)$, $\mathbf{Ch}(X)$, $\mathbf{An}(X)$, and $\mathbf{De}(X)$, respectively.

:::



::: {#def-intervention .theorem}
# Intervention

An operation on an NPSEM-IE which amends or replaces some structural equations. Two kinds: a *node intervention* fixes values used by downstream equations; an *edge intervention* replaces one or more structural equations with experimenter-specified functions.

$$
f_V\mapsto f_V^{(\mathrm{g})}
$$
:::

::: {#def-counterfactual-npsem .theorem}
# Counterfactual NPSEM-IE

A counterfactual NPSEM-IE is an NPSEM-IE that has undergone an intervention.


$$
V_{j}^{(\mathbf{g})}  \;=\; f_{j}^*\!\big( V_{1}^{(\mathbf{g})},\dots,V_{j-1}^{(\mathbf{g})},\, U_{j} \big),
$$

$$
\{U_j\}_{j=1}^p \ \text{ mutually independent.}
$$

:::





::: {#def-no-spillover .theorem}
## No spillover assumption

In an [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie), the *no spillover* assumption requires that no variable is a [parent](#def-parent-child) of an [equivalent](#def-equivalence) variable in another [observational unit](#def-observational-unit).

$$
X\notin \mathbf{Pa}(X')\quad
\forall\, X\sim X',\ X\in \mathbf V_i,\ X'\in \mathbf V_j,\ i\ne j.
$$
:::

::: {#def-no-interference .theorem}
## No interference assumption

In an [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie), the *no interference* assumption requires that no variable is a [parent](#def-parent-child) of any non-[equivalent](#def-equivalence) variable in another [observational unit](#def-observational-unit).

$$
X\notin \mathbf{Pa}(Y)\quad
\forall\, X\in \mathbf V_i,\ Y\in \mathbf V_j,\ i\ne j,\ X\not\sim Y.
$$
:::

::: {#def-identical-distributions .theorem}
## Identical distributions assumption

In an [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie), the *identical distributions* assumption requires that [equivalent](#def-equivalence) variables have equivalent sets of [parents](#def-parent-child) and identical structural equations.

$$
X_i\sim X_j\Rightarrow f_{X_i}=f_{X_j}.
$$
:::

::: {#def-ffrcistg .theorem}
## FFRCISTG model

A *[finest fully randomized causally interpretable structured tree graph (FFRCISTG) model](#def-ffrcistg)* is a collection of [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie) models constructed for the purpose of examinig a causal question. One representing the observed NPSEM-IE and a set representing counterfactual NPSEM-IE derived through intervening on the observed data NPSEM-IE. We assume the error term for each variable is equal, regardless of the model.

Each [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie) in the collection satisfies the (1) [no spillover](#def-no-spillover), (2) [no interference](#def-no-interference), and (3) [identical distributions](#def-identical-distributions) assumptions. 

$$
\mathcal C=\{\mathscr M^{(a)}:a\in\mathcal A\},\quad
\mathscr M^{(\emptyset)}\text{ observed},\quad
\forall a\in\mathcal A:\ \mathscr M^{(a)}\text{ satisfies (1)–(3)}.
$$
:::

#### Network causal inference


::: {#def-graph .theorem}
## Graph

A *[graph](#def-graph)* is an ordered pair $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$ with nodeset $\mathcal{N}$ a countable set and adjacency function $\psi : \mathcal{N} \times \mathcal{N} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ which assigns a nonnegative weight to each unordered pair of nodes. Nodes $i,j \in \mathcal{N}$ are connected if and only if $\psi(i,j) > 0$.

$$
\mathscr G=(\mathcal N,\psi),\qquad
\psi:\mathcal N\times\mathcal N\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0},\qquad
\psi(i,j)=\psi(j,i)
$$
:::


::: {#def-neighborhood .theorem}
## Neighborhood

Given a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$, the *[neighborhood](#def-neighborhood)* of a node $i \in \mathcal{N}$ is

$$
\mathcal{N}_i = \{ j \in \mathcal{N} : \psi(i,j) > 0 \}.
$$
:::

::: {#def-network-weights-vector .theorem}
## Network weights 

Given a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$, the *[network weights vector](#def-network-weights-vector)* for a node $i \in \mathcal{N}$ is

$$
\Psi_i = [\psi(i,1), \dots, \psi(i,n)]^T,
\qquad n=|\mathcal N|.
$$
:::

::: {#def-network-values .theorem}
## Network values 

Given a vector $\mathbf{X} \in \{0,1\}^n$ indexed by nodes of a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G}=(\mathcal{N},\psi)$ with neighborhood $\mathcal N_i$ for node $i$, the *network values* for node $i$ with respect to $\mathbf X$ is the subvector of $\mathbf X$ indexed by $\mathcal N_i$.

$$
\mathbf X_{\mathcal N_i}=\big(X_j\big)_{j\in \mathcal N_i}.
$$
:::

::: {#def-exposure-mapping .theorem}
## Exposure mapping

Given an [NPSEM-IE](#def-npsem-ie) with $f_{Y_i}$ the structural equation for $Y_i$, and $\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_K \in \{0,1\}^n$ the [parents](#def-parent-child) of $Y_i$, the *[exposure mapping](#def-exposure-mapping) for $f_{Y_i}$* is a function

$$
g_i : \{0,1\}^{K \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^m
$$

such that

$$
Y_i = f_{Y_i}\big(g_i(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_K), U_{Y_i}\big).
$$
:::

::: {#def-separability .theorem}
## Separability

An [exposure mapping](#def-exposure-mapping) $g_i$ is *[separable](#def-separability)* if it decomposes as

$$
g_i(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_K) 
  = \big[g_{0},\, g_{1i}(\mathbf{X}_1),\, \dots,\, g_{Ki}(\mathbf{X}_K)\big]^T,
$$

where $g_{0} = [X_{1i}, \dots, X_{Ki}]^T$, and each $g_{ti} : \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a *component function* of $g_i$. A structural equation is said to be separable if its exposure mapping is separable. 
:::

::: {#def-loyalty .theorem}
## Loyalty

Given a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$, let $\mathcal{N}_i$ denote the [neighborhood](#def-neighborhood) of node $i$. A [component function](#def-separability) $g_{ti}$ is *[loyal](#def-loyalty)* to $\mathscr{G}$ if for all $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{X}' \in \{0,1\}^n$, such that

$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{X}'_{\mathcal{N}_i}
\Rightarrow
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) = g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}').
$$

An exposure mapping is loyal to $\mathscr{G}$ if it is separable and all its component functions are loyal to $\mathscr{G}$. A structural equation is said to be loyal if its exposure mapping is loyal.
:::

::: {#def-positional-invariance .theorem}
## Positional invariance

Given a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$, let $\mathcal{N}_i$ and vectors $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{X'} \in \{0,1\}^n$, a [component function](#def-separability) $g_{ti}$ is *[positionally invariant](#def-positional-invariance)* if for nodes $i,j \in \mathcal{N}$, there exists a conformable permutation matrix $\mathbf{M}$ such that

$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\mathbf{X}'_{\mathcal{N}_j}, 
\quad 
\Psi_{i,\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\Psi_{j,\mathcal{N}_j}
\Rightarrow
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) = g_{tj}(\mathbf{X}').
$$

An exposure mapping shows positional invariance with respect to $\mathscr{G}$ if it is separable and all its component functions show positional invariance. A structural equation is positionally invariant if its exposure mapping is positionally invariant. 
:::

::: {#def-boundedness .theorem}
## Boundedness

A [component function](#def-separability) $g_{ti}$ is *[bounded](#def-boundedness)* if there exists a finite set $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathbb{R}$ and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$, independent of the size of the network $|\mathcal{N}|$, such that

$$
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{W}) \in \mathcal{D}, \quad \text{for all } \mathbf{X} \in \{0,1\}^n,\ \mathbf{W} \in \mathbb{R}^n_+,
\qquad |\mathcal{D}|<c.
$$

An exposure mapping is bounded if it is separable and all its component functions are bounded. 
:::

::: {#def-homogeneous-network-interference .theorem}
## Network exposure mappings and values



:::

::: {#def-homogeneous-network-interference .theorem}
## Homogeneous network interference

An exposure mapping exhibits *[homogeneous network interference](#def-homogeneous-network-interference)* with respect to a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G}$ if it is separable, bounded, positionally invariant, and loyal to $\mathscr{G}$. An NPSEM-IE exhibits homogeneous network interference if all its exposure mappings do.

:::



::: {#def-network-ffrcistg .theorem}
## Network FFRCISTG model

A *[network FFRCISTG model](#def-network-ffrcistg)* is a [FFRCISTG model](#def-ffrcistg) in which the underlying [NPSEM-IEs](#def-npsem-ie) exhibit no spillover, homogeneous network interference with respect to $\mathscr{G}$, and identical distributions. 


:::

#### Social and spatial inference

::: {#def-random-nodes-bipartite-graph .theorem}
## Random graph generator

A structural equation that produces the adjacency function (matrix) of a bipartite graph with conformable dimensions.

$$
f_\psi:\mathcal U\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{|V_1|\times |V_2|},
\qquad
\psi = f_\psi(U_\psi),\quad \operatorname{supp}(\psi)\subseteq V_1\times V_2 \cup V_2\times V_1.
$$
:::

::: {#def-social-spatial-npsem .theorem}
## Random graph NPSEM-IE

An NPSEM-IE whose structural equations include random graph generators whose component functions are loyal to one or more random graphs included in the model.

$$
\mathscr M=\{f_V:V\in\mathbf V\}\cup\{f_\psi\},\qquad
\text{each }g_{ti}\text{ in exposure mappings is loyal to the generated graphs.}
$$
:::

::: {#def-homogeneous-network-interference .theorem}
## Homogeneous random network interference

In a random graph NPSEM-IE, an exposure mapping exhibits homogeneous random network interference if it is separable and bounded and each of its component functions is loyal to a random graph included in the model.

:::

::: {#def-social-spatial-ffrcistg .theorem}
## Random network FFRCISTG

A FFRCISTG in which the NPSEM-IEs satisfy: (i) no spillover (optionally exempting graph generators), (ii) homogeneous random network interference, and (iii) identical distributions.


:::

::: {#def-bipartite-graph .theorem}
## Bipartite graph

A *[bipartite graph](#def-bipartite-graph)* is a [graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$ defined by the following conditions:

1. *Partition:* $\mathcal{N} = V_1 \cup V_2$ with $V_1 \cap V_2 = \varnothing$.  
2. *Restricted adjacency:* $\psi$ is supported only across the partition.

$$
\mathcal N=V_1\cup V_2,\quad V_1\cap V_2=\varnothing,\qquad
\psi(i,j)>0\Rightarrow (i,j)\in V_1\times V_2\ \text{or}\ (i,j)\in V_2\times V_1.
$$
:::

::: {#def-bipartite-npsem .theorem}
## Bipartite random graph NPSEM-IE

A random graph NPSEM-IE where all generated graphs are bipartite.

$$
f_\psi:\mathcal U\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{|V_1|\times |V_2|},\qquad
\operatorname{supp}(\psi)\subseteq V_1\times V_2\cup V_2\times V_1.
$$
:::

::: {#def-social-spatial-ffrcistg .theorem}
## Bipartite random network FFRCISTG model

A FFRCISTG with NPSEM-IEs that (i) have no spillover (including for graph generators), (ii) satisfy homogeneous random network interference, and (iii) maintain identical distributions.

$$
\mathcal C=\{\mathscr M^{(a)}\},\qquad
\forall a:\ \text{no spillover} \wedge \text{HRNI} \wedge \text{identical distributions},\quad
\text{with bipartite graph generators}.
$$
:::
